newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close week at year high.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close week at year high.

text.p: French shares surged almost one percent in afternoon trading on Friday to finish at a year high.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 21.90 points or 0.98 percent at 2,255.47 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 20.5 at 2,259 from Thursday's close.
Operators cited positive trends in bonds, Wall Street and a recovery in the franc.
Total volume was a hefty 7.3 billion francs.
U.S. funds were significant buyers, the head of equity sales at a big French brokerage said.

Around one billion francs went through on insurers Axa and UAP combined. Axa closed up 2.38 percent at 314.4 francs, while UAP firmed 1.45 percent at 139.8. Axa's merger offer for UAP shares opened on Thursday.

Heavy trading in oils Elf and Total and engineering group Alcatel Alsthom made up a further billion francs. Elf firmed 1.71 percent to 457.9 francs, Total up 1.74 percent to 421, as crude prices continued to climb.
Elf sold 10 percent of French firm Geophysique.
Beauty products group Dior accounted for 200 million francs in volume, and closed up 1.25 percent at 731 francs.
Virtually all the activity was in blue chips. The CAC-40 index has gained 3.58 percent on the month.
"UAP-Axa started things off," said one broker. The merger, often denied despite persistent rumours, has rekindled intense speculation in takeovers in the financial and other sectors.
Paribas is often cited as a target for link-ups. The holding company closed up 0.03 percent at 360 francs.
Retailers Casino and Promodes are seen as potential partners, despite denials.
